themes.consensus_view: Most desks see the AI trade as dangerously crowded and stretched, with concentration and leverage at bubble-like extremes, even as a couple of banks note the hardware/capex boom still has momentum.

facts_agreed.claim: The AI trade is extremely concentrated and stretched, sitting near historical bubble thresholds.
evidence_quotes: AI is now 39% of SPX, or at the ceiling of bubble concentration
Nasdaq's Bubble Risk Indicator closer to the critical 0.8 level

facts_agreed.claim: The AI-driven boom is showing signs of fragility, with extreme leverage and crowded positioning straining the trade.
evidence_quotes: The market is no longer behaving as if risk does not exist.
The leverage embedded in the market has become so extreme
both consumption and investment are dependent on the AI ‘bubble’ not bursting
A leveraged unwind in AI-linked equities drove a risk-off rotation into the dollar

facts_contested.claim: whether the AI/hardware trade still has upside
facts_contested.for_evidence: Until that changes, the hardware trade likely remains in vogue.
facts_contested.against_evidence: it is getting harder to justify further large gains

themes.consensus_view: Most banks read new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish debut as a shift toward keeping interest rates higher, with markets now pricing one more hike and modest extra tightening into 2027, though one desk warns markets are still underestimating how hard the Fed could go.

facts_agreed.claim: New FOMC Chair Kevin Warsh opened with a hawkish stance that markets are interpreting as a shift toward tighter policy.
evidence_quotes: quite the flip from the consensus assumptions six months ago
Investors have modestly reduced their risk-seeking behaviour following a hawkish debut by new FOMC Chair
the market has projected a hawkish Fed rate path

facts_contested.claim: whether markets have correctly priced the Fed's hawkishness
facts_contested.for_evidence: A pivot to a more appropriate policy stance is acting as a volatility suppressor.
facts_contested.against_evidence: I think the danger is that if the generic “Iran Deal” gives Warsh a pass

themes.consensus_view: Six trading desks flag US-Iran peace talks as a live near-term market catalyst, but none has staked out a directional view on whether a deal closes.

facts_agreed.claim: Six banks reference US-Iran talks as an active near-term catalyst, framing it around progress toward a settlement or ceasefire without staking a directional call.

themes.consensus_view: Several banks track Strait of Hormuz oil flows as a live supply story, with shipping still running well below pre-war levels but no shared directional call on how fast it recovers.

facts_agreed.claim: Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain well below pre-war levels and would need a large increase to fully recover.
Multiple desks are monitoring Strait of Hormuz traffic and oil-flow conditions as an active macro input.

themes.consensus_view: One desk sees biotech turning higher, pointing to fresh price highs and a renewed wave of buyouts, but no other bank has staked a view to confirm or challenge it.

facts_agreed.claim: Biotech is breaking out technically, with the sector printing fresh 52-week highs alongside a renewed wave of acquisitions.
